arxiv-2203-03203.title: Constraints on self-dual black hole in loop quantum gravity with S0-2 star in the Galactic Center
arxiv-2203-03203.creator: Jian-Ming Yan a,b, Qiang Wu a,b, Cheng Liu a,b, Tao Zhu a,b, Anzhong Wang c
arxiv-2203-03203.description: Abstract One of remarkable features of loop quantum gravity (LQG) is that it can provide resolutions to both the black hole and big bang singularities. In the mini-superspace approach based on the polymerization procedure in LQG, a quantum corrected black hole metric is constructed.

arxiv-2212-12621.title: Nothing Stands Alone: Relational Fake News Detection with Hypergraph Neural Networks
arxiv-2212-12621.creator: Ujun Jeong 1 , Kaize Ding 1 , Lu Cheng 2 , Ruocheng Guo 3 , Kai Shu 4 and Huan Liu 1
arxiv-2212-12621.description: Abstract Nowadays, fake news easily propagates through online social networks and becomes a grand threat to individuals and society. Assessing the authenticity of news is challenging due to its elaborately fabricated contents, making it difficult to obtain large-scale annotations for fake news data.

arxiv-2304-07649.title: Proposed Resolution to the Solar Open Magnetic Flux Problem
arxiv-2304-07649.creator: C. Nick Arge, Andrew Leisner, Samantha Wallace, Carl J. Henney
arxiv-2304-07649.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by C. Nick Arge, Andrew Leisner, Samantha Wallace, Carl J. Henney. The solar magnetic fields emerging from the photosphere into the chromosphere and corona are comprised of a combination of “closed” and “open” fields. The closed magnetic field lines are defined as those having both ends rooted in the solar surface, while the “open” field lines are those having one end extending out into interplanetary space and the other rooted at the Sun’s surface.

arxiv-2308-12724.title: Jet energy calibration with deep learning as a Kubeflow pipeline
arxiv-2308-12724.creator: Daniel Holmberg, Dejan Golubovic, Henning Kirschenmann
arxiv-2308-12724.description: Abstract Precise measurements of the energy of jets emerging from particle collisions at the LHC are essential for a vast majority of physics searches at the CMS experiment. In this study, we leverage well-established deep learning models for point clouds and CMS open data to improve the energy calibration of particle jets.

arxiv-2311-14096.title: Cultural Bias and Cultural Alignment of Large Language Models
arxiv-2311-14096.creator: Yan Tao, Olga Viberg, Ryan S. Baker, René F. Kizilcec
arxiv-2311-14096.description: Abstract Culture fundamentally shapes people’s reasoning, behavior, and communication. As people increasingly use generative artificial intelligence (AI) to expedite and automate personal and professional tasks, cultural values embedded in AI models may bias people’s authentic expression and contribute to the dominance of certain cultures.

arxiv-2401-12623.title: A Unifying System Theory Framework for Distributed Optimization and Games
arxiv-2401-12623.creator: Guido Carnevale, Nicola Mimmo, Giuseppe Notarstefano
arxiv-2401-12623.description: Abstract This paper introduces a systematic methodological framework to design and analyze distributed algorithms for optimization and games over networks. Starting from a centralized method, we identify an aggregation function involving all the decision variables (e.g., a global cost gradient or constraint) and introduce a distributed consensus-oriented scheme to asymptotically approximate the unavailable information at each agent.

arxiv-2404-10682.title: Characterization of the multimode nature of single-photon sources based on spontaneous parametric down conversion
arxiv-2404-10682.creator: Emil R. Hellebek, Klaus Mølmer, Anders S. Sørensen
arxiv-2404-10682.description: Abstract Single-photon sources are necessary components for many prospective quantum technologies. One candidate for a single-photon source is spontaneous parametric down conversion combined with a heralding photon detection. The heralded light pulse from such a source, is typically treated as single-mode, this treatment, however, is incomplete.

arxiv-2406-06041.title: Risk Sensitivity in Markov Games and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: A Systematic Review
arxiv-2406-06041.creator: Hafez Ghaemi, Shirin Jamshidi, Mohammad Mashreghi, Majid Nili Ahmadabadi, Hamed Kebriaei, Senior Member, IEEE
arxiv-2406-06041.description: Abstract Markov games (MGs) and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) are studied to model decision making in multi-agent systems. Traditionally, the objective in MG and MARL has been risk-neutral, i.e., agents are assumed to optimize a performance metric such as expected return, without taking into account subjective or cognitive preferences of themselves or of other agents.

arxiv-2407-07050.title: Interplay between Majorana and Shiba states in a minimal Kitaev chain coupled to a superconductor
arxiv-2407-07050.creator: M. Alvarado ID, A. Levy Yeyati ID, Ramón Aguado ID, R. Seoane Souto ID
arxiv-2407-07050.description: Abstract Two semiconducting quantum dots (QDs) coupled through a superconductor constitute a minimal realisation of a Kitaev chain with Majorana zero modes (MZMs). Such MZMs can be detected by e.g. , tunneling conductance between each QD and normal leads [ Dvir et al, Nature 614 , 445 (2023) ].

arxiv-2410-14267.title: Algebraic constructions of cubic minimal cones
arxiv-2410-14267.creator: Daniel J. F. Fox, Vladimir G. Tkachev
arxiv-2410-14267.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Daniel J. F. Fox, Vladimir G. Tkachev. Hsiang algebras are a class of nonassociative algebra defined in terms of a relation quartic in elements of the algebra. This class arises naturally in relation to the construction of real algebraic minimal cones. Additionally, Hsiang algebras were crucial in the construction of singular (trulsy viscosity) solutions of nonlinear uniformly elliptic partial differential equations in a series of papers by Nikolai Nadirashvili and Serge Vlăduţ.

arxiv-2503-19157.title: HOIGPT: Learning Long-Sequence Hand-Object Interaction with Language Models
arxiv-2503-19157.creator: Mingzhen Huang, Fu-Jen Chu, Bugra Tekin, Kevin J. Liang, Haoyu Ma, Weiyao Wang, Xingyu Chen, Pierre Gleize, Hongfei Xue, Siwei Lyu, Kris Kitani, Matt Feiszli, Hao Tang
arxiv-2503-19157.description: Abstract We introduce HOIGPT, a token-based generative method that unifies 3D hand-object interactions (HOI) perception and generation, offering the first comprehensive solution for captioning and generating high-quality 3D HOI sequences from a diverse range of conditional signals ( e.g . text, objects, partial sequences).

arxiv-2602-19362.title: LLMs Can Learn to Reason Via Off-Policy RL
arxiv-2602-19362.creator: Daniel Ritter, Owen Oertell, Bradley Guo, Jonathan D. Chang, Kianté Brantley, Wen Sun
arxiv-2602-19362.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) approaches for Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently use on-policy algorithms, such as PPO or GRPO. However, policy lag from distributed training architectures and differences between the training and inference policies break this assumption, making the data off-policy by design.

plos-pone-0003400.description: PLOS ONE research article. We developed a composite machine-learning based algorithm, called ANGLOR, to predict real-value protein backbone torsion angles from amino acid sequences. The input features of ANGLOR include sequence profiles, predicted secondary structure and solvent accessibility. In a large-s

pmc-11588397.creator: Irfan Khan, Matthew B. Lanktree
pmc-11588397.description: neous semaglutide reduced the relative risk of kidney failure, 50% decline in eGFR, or death by 24%.1 A meta-analysis of 64 286 patients showed that GLP-1 receptor agonists reduced the relative risk of all-cause death by 12% compared with placebo.

pmc-11657349.title: Association between bowel movement frequency, stool consistency and MAFLD and advanced fibrosis in US adults: a cross-sectional study of NHANES 2005-2010
pmc-11657349.creator: Miaomin Ye, Yijia He, Yin Xia, Ziyi Zhong, Xiaocen Kong, Yunting Zhou, Weiping Wang, Suping Qin, Qian Li
pmc-11657349.description: BackgroundAlthough previous studies have established associations between specific gut microbiota (GM) and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), research examining the relationship between functional gastrointestinal symptoms and MAFLD, including advanced fibrosis, remains limited. This study aims to investigate the association between stool consistency, bowel movement frequency (BMF), and the occurrence of MAFLD and advanced fibrosis in U.S. adults.

pmc-12489277.title: Toward understanding apoplastic freezing under negative pressure
pmc-12489277.creator: Stephen Ingram, Alessandro Zanetti, Linnea Mustonen, Ana A Piedehierro, Ari Laaksonen, Anna Lintunen
pmc-12489277.description: Summary The impact of negative liquid pressure on the freezing of xylem sap is a unique scientific problem. Equilibrium thermodynamics would suggest that, due to the density anomaly of ice, sap under tension should freeze at higher temperatures than under positive pressure. Yet, the opposite is observed in tree branches: freezing temperatures decrease as the pressure becomes more negative.

pmc-12578649.title: Comparison of One-Year Adverse Events Between First- and Second-Generation Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Retrospective Study
pmc-12578649.creator: Ao Ito, Kaori Ito, Chisako Iriyama, Naoe Goto, Yoshihiro Inamoto, Masataka Okamoto, Yuichi Hirose, Misaki Morisaku, Shigeki Yamada, Nobuki Hayakawa, Akihiro Tomita
pmc-12578649.description: Background/Aim: Bruton’s tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKi) are important targeted agents for hematological malignancies. Second-generation BTKi are considered to have fewer off-target enzyme effects than first-generation agents; however, real-world comparative data on adverse events (AEs) remain limited. AEs of special interest with BTKi include bone marrow suppression, infection, hemorrhage, and cardiac-related events.

pmc-12589515.title: On the multi-objective hyperparameter optimization of the weighted entropic associative memory
pmc-12589515.creator: Juan Antonio López Rivera, Carlos Ignacio Hernández Castellanos, Rafael Morales, Luis A. Pineda Cortés
pmc-12589515.description: This paper presents an application of automatic algorithm configuration to optimize the performance of the Weighted Entropic Associative Memory (W-EAM). This model holds declarative but distributed representations of remembered objects. We apply two state-of-the-art hyperparameter tuning methods—SMAC and SMS-EMOA—to improve W-EAM’s recognition accuracy across three domains of increasing complexity: digit recognition, character recognition, and phone recognition in Mexican Spanish.

pmc-13027856.title: A Hierarchical Multi-View Deep Learning Framework for Autism Classification Using Structural and Functional MRI
pmc-13027856.creator: Nayif Mohammed Hammash, Mohammed Chachan Younis
pmc-13027856.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Autism classification is challenging due to the subtle, heterogeneous, and overlapping neural activation profiles that occur in individuals with autism. Novel deep learning approaches, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and their variants, as well as Transformers, have shown moderate performance in discriminating between autism and normal cohorts; yet, they often struggle to jointly capture the spatial–structural and temporal–functional variations present in autistic brains.

pmc-13198369.title: Growth performance, blood composition, carcass characteristics, and meat quality of Ossimi and Barki fattening lambs as influenced by breed type and zilpaterol hydrochloride supplementation
pmc-13198369.creator: Ahmed M A Hussein, Mahmoud M Abdelsattar, Einar Vargas-Bello-Pérez, Yanliang Bi
pmc-13198369.description: To study the effect of zilpaterol hydrochloride (ZH), 60 lambs were divided into six groups of different breeds (Ossimi or Barki) receiving 0 [CON], 0.10 [Z1], or 0.15 [Z2] mg/kg BW. Ossimi had higher feed intake, carcass traits, blood hemoglobin, and neutrophils, but lower meat protein and blood basophils.

pmc-13247179.title: Short-term pretreatment with deferoxamine enhances the in vivo vascularization capacity of nanofat seeded onto dermal substitutes
pmc-13247179.creator: Valeria Pruzzo, Francesca Bonomi, Ettore Limido, Andrea Weinzierl, Yves Harder, Matthias W Laschke
pmc-13247179.description: Insufficient early vascularization remains a major limitation for the successful integration of implanted dermal substitutes. To overcome this challenge, nanofat has recently been introduced as a promising fat derivative for implant seeding. The present study investigated whether short-term ex vivo pretreatment with the hypoxia-mimetic agent deferoxamine (DFO) can further enhance the in vivo vascularization capacity of nanofat.

pmc-13346984.title: Coupling of the finite element limit equilibrium method with the stochastic search algorithm and its application for an embankment dam
pmc-13346984.creator: Juraj Ŝtetiar, Juraj Chalmovský
pmc-13346984.description: Slope stability analysis is a crucial task in the design of geotechnical structures. In many computational methods, such as those combining displacement-based finite element methods and strength reduction techniques, no assumptions are made a priori about the shape or position of the failure mechanism.

pmc-13380757.title: A rapid point-of-care test for vancomycin monitoring at the clinical bedside
pmc-13380757.creator: Damon T. Burrow, David S. Kinnamon, Jason Liu, Jacob T. Heggestad, Simone Wall, Brooke E. Silverstein, Suhail K. Mithani, Vijay Krishnamoorthy, Richard Drew, Daniel Y. Joh, Angus Hucknall, Ashutosh Chilkoti
pmc-13380757.description: SummaryVancomycin requires individualized dosing guided by therapeutic drug monitoring, but current laboratory assays are slow and centralized. We describe a competition-format microarray assay on a poly(oligo(ethylene glycol) methacrylate-co-glycidyl methacrylate) brush integrated into a single-use microfluidic cassette and portable reader to quantify vancomycin directly from fingerstick volumes of whole blood in 30 min.

pmc-13534176.title: Cardiac implantable electronic devices in heart failure: needs, challenges, and real-world implementation
pmc-13534176.creator: David Žižek, Miha Mrak, Anja Zupan Mežnar, Maja Ivanovski, Tadej Žlahtič, Christopher F Barrientos, Andrew P Ambrosy, Zlatko Fras, Mauro Biffi, Mitja Lainscak
pmc-13534176.description: Cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) are integral to heart failure (HF) management, providing therapies for bradyarrhythmias, cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), sudden cardiac death (SCD) prevention, and remote monitoring. This review summarizes current and potential future indications, emerging technologies, and challenges in the implementation of CIEDs in HF.

pmc-13574990.title: Decoupling Fabrication From Encoding: DNA‐Addressable Template Microparticles for Large, User‐Defined Optical Barcode Libraries
pmc-13574990.creator: Akihiro Eguchi, Yuichiro Iwamoto, Hinata Tokuda, Haruka Narita, Adrian M. Martin, Sadao Ota
pmc-13574990.description: Optical barcodes for pooled high‐throughput screening must support large libraries while remaining decodable in a single imaging step. Existing approaches often trade design control for manufacturability: deterministic barcodes often require per‐code redesign of particle fabrication, whereas stochastic combinatorial barcodes are difficult to generate as predefined batches.

pmc-13578187.title: N-terminal lipidation enhances membrane interaction and antifungal activity of a Trematocine-derived decapeptide
pmc-13578187.creator: Damiano Squitieri, Federica Massaro, Melinda Mariotti, Margherita Cacaci, Stefano Borocci, Fernando Porcelli, Francesco Buonocore, Francesca Bugli, Maurizio Sanguinetti
pmc-13578187.description: AbstractInvasive fungal infections are a growing global health threat, driven by the limited availability of antifungal therapies and the rapid spread of multidrug-resistant yeasts. This study explored the effects of N-terminal lipidation on Trem-4, a decapeptide derived from the antimicrobial peptide Trematocine-HSK, to enhance its antifungal potential.

pmc-13647548.title: Optimizing stroke mortality prediction: a comparative study of sampling, cost-sensitive learning, and threshold adjustment
pmc-13647548.creator: Rahim Nikbakht-Fard, Leili Tapak, Mojtaba Khazei, Elaheh Talebi-Ghane
pmc-13647548.description: BackgroundStroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide, creating a critical need for accurate prediction tools to support early clinical decision making. However, mortality prediction is often hindered by class imbalance, as death events represent a minority of cases in most clinical datasets.
